items.followUp: What is geophysics, and how does it help us study the Earth?

rubric.why: Identifies the subject and its focus.
rubric.description: Names geophysics as the study of the Earth using physics.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying geophysics and its focus on the Earth.

rubric.why: States the role of physics in this field.
rubric.description: Explains that geophysics applies physics or its principles to the study of the Earth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the application of physics.

modelAnswer: Geophysics is the branch of physics that applies the principles of physics to study the Earth.

items.followUp: Estimate the number of seconds in 12 years. Take 1 year as 365 days.

rubric.why: Shows the conversion from years to seconds using the number of days in a year.
rubric.description: Uses 15 years and converts years, days, hours, minutes, and seconds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct conversion setup.

rubric.why: Gives the estimated age in seconds.
rubric.description: Calculates the age as approximately 4.73 × 10⁸ seconds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct answer with a unit.

modelAnswer: Given: Age = 15 years; 1 year = 365 days.
Time in seconds = 15 × 365 × 24 × 60 × 60 s.
Time in seconds = 473,040,000 s ≈ 4.73 × 10⁸ s.

items.followUp: Define centripetal force and state its direction for a body moving in a circle.

rubric.why: Identifies centrifugal force as an apparent or experienced force in circular motion.
rubric.description: Defines centrifugal force as the apparent force on a body moving in a circular path.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as an apparent force associated with circular motion.

rubric.why: Gives the defining direction of centrifugal force.
rubric.description: States that centrifugal force is directed away from the centre of the circular path.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the direction away from the centre.

modelAnswer: Centrifugal force is the apparent force experienced by a body moving in a circular path.
It acts radially outward, away from the centre of the circular path.

items.followUp: State two properties of the action–reaction forces described by Newton’s third law.

rubric.why: States the paired forces’ relative magnitudes and directions.
rubric.description: Action and reaction are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the forces are equal and opposite.

rubric.why: Distinguishes the pair by where the forces act.
rubric.description: Action and reaction act on two different bodies, so they do not cancel each other.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they act on different bodies.

modelAnswer: Action and reaction are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.
They act simultaneously on two different bodies, so they do not cancel each other.

items.followUp: In a distance–time graph, identify the independent and dependent variables.

rubric.why: Provides the meaning of a graph.
rubric.description: Defines a graph as a visual or pictorial representation of the relationship between variables.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining a graph as a representation of a relationship between variables.

rubric.why: Identifies which variable is set or chosen and which responds to it.
rubric.description: The independent variable is chosen or controlled; the dependent variable changes in response to it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly distinguishing both variables.

modelAnswer: A graph is a pictorial representation of the relationship between two variables.
The independent variable is chosen or controlled and is plotted on the horizontal axis.
The dependent variable changes in response to the independent variable and is plotted on the vertical axis.

items.followUp: Draw a distance–time graph for a body moving with constant speed.

rubric.why: Shows the variables on the appropriate axes.
rubric.description: Labels time on the horizontal axis and distance on the vertical axis, with units and a stated scale.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly labelled axes and a usable scale.

rubric.why: A body at rest remains at one fixed distance as time passes.
rubric.description: Plots points at the same distance for all times and joins them with a horizontal line.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a horizontal distance–time line representing constant distance.

modelAnswer: Choose the scale: horizontal axis 1 cm = 1 s; vertical axis 1 cm = 1 m.
Table of values: time t (s): 0, 1, 2, 3, 4; distance d (m): 2, 2, 2, 2, 2.
Draw and label the horizontal time axis t (s) and vertical distance axis d (m).
Plot (0 s, 2 m), (1 s, 2 m), (2 s, 2 m), (3 s, 2 m), and (4 s, 2 m); join them with a horizontal line at d = 2 m.

items.followUp: A sample has a mass of 600 g and a volume of 300 cm³. Find its density in kg/m³.

rubric.why: Converts the measurements to SI units.
rubric.description: Converts 400 g to 0.4 kg and 200 cm³ to 2 × 10⁻⁴ m³.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct SI conversions.

rubric.why: Applies density = mass ÷ volume and obtains the correct SI result.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula, substitution, and answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: mass m = 400 g = 0.4 kg; volume V = 200 cm³ = 2 × 10⁻⁴ m³.
Formula: density ρ = m/V.
Substitution: ρ = 0.4 kg ÷ (2 × 10⁻⁴ m³).
Answer: ρ = 2000 kg/m³.

items.followUp: Define a couple and state the angle between the two forces forming it.

rubric.why: Identifies the equal and opposite forces that form a couple.
rubric.description: A couple consists of two equal, opposite, parallel forces acting at different points.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the defining force pair.

rubric.why: Gives the angle between the opposite forces.
rubric.description: The angle between the two forces of a couple is 180°.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct angle.

modelAnswer: A couple consists of two equal, parallel forces acting in opposite directions at different points on a body.
The angle between the two forces is 180°.
